notes: Large 20-part sheet with NO GND symbol anywhere, so no net is named 0; the four V-DC (one port) arrows are supply taps (+18 V = id 15, +15 V = id 17, +6 V = id 13, +5 V = id 18) and are treated as ordinary single-terminal nodes. Coordinates are in the 512x512 image. CROSSOVER CONVENTION: this drafter marks a crossing by making one wire take a short rectangular/semicircular DETOUR whose apex lies on the wire being crossed (the same style as the hops in circuits 1209/1233). Two such detours exist here and both were confirmed pixel by pixel; every other meeting in the sheet is a corner, a T, or a dotted junction. Net map: n1 = the long left rail, the vertical at x=39-43 from the top-left corner (40,58) down to (40,492) where it turns right into BJT 3's emitter. It T-joins the emitters of BJT 9 (41,89), BJT 14 (42,249), BJT 8 (42,375) and BJT 3, carries the top rail off its top corner into R4's left lead, and at (43,307) sends the horizontal that runs right to R2's left lead. n2 = the clean vertical at x=87-90 from BJT 9's base bar (86,108) straight down to BJT 14's base bar (92,234) - no branches. n3 = BJT 9's collector, up-right then right along y=93-98 to BJT 1's emitter at (232,98). n4 = the +18 V node: R4's right lead -> (241,47) -> (285,46), where a T sends one branch down to (285,67) and left along y=66 to (249,66) and down into BJT 1's BASE, while the main line runs on to (360,42) -> the +18 V arrow (V-DC 15) and down the x=360 vertical to (360,92) on the R7/R12 chain. Judgment calls: (a) THE CRITICAL ONE: at (92,312) the left-rail horizontal steps down from (87,307), runs right to x=97 at y=313 and steps back up to y=306, straddling the x=91-92 vertical symmetrically (descent starts 5 px left of it, ascent 5 px right). This is the drafter's detour-hop, identical in construction to the confirmed hop at (308,331) where the diode line dips from (302,324) to y=331 and back up at (315,324) across the x=308 vertical. I therefore read it as a CROSSING: the horizontal carries the left rail through to R2, and the vertical (BJT 14 collector -> BJT 8 base, n9) passes under it untouched. Reading it as a junction instead would short BJT 14 collector-to-emitter through the left rail and would merge n1 with n9 - a strong argument that the hop reading is right, but a re-checker should look here first. (b) All eight BJTs were zoomed to 11-16x. Every one is drawn with a thick base bar, a single lead perpendicular to it (the base), and two slanted leads; the lead carrying the arrowhead was taken as the emitter and terminals were ordered [collector, base, emitter]. Base direction: BJT 9 and BJT 0 have their base lead pointing DOWN; BJT 1, 3, 8, 14, 16, 19 point UP. Arrow senses in this sheet are not drawn consistently with the NPN/PNP labels supplied in the inventory (e.g. id 9 is labelled NPN but its arrow points toward the base), so I identified the emitter purely by which lead carries the arrowhead and left every class unchanged. (c) Both diodes are drawn bar-on-the-left with the triangle pointing left, so index 0 is the cathode lead and index 1 the anode lead; 2-terminal order does not affect any metric. (d) Resistor orientation: R2, R4, R7 and R12 are horizontal (index 0 = left lead), R5 and R10 are vertical (index 0 = top). (e) The R7/R12 chain is one horizontal: BJT 1 collector -> R7 -> node n4 at x=360 -> R12 -> right rail. The central column hangs off the left end of that chain at x=306, i.e. on R7's left terminal, not on the n4 node. (f) The bootstrap file was almost entirely wrong here - it named six resistor terminals '0' although the sheet contains no ground symbol at all, and left 30 of the 44 terminals null; every value was re-derived from the drawing.
